minor.issue: Mixes a reviewer note (the abstract vs results discrepancy) into the authors' limitations. Useful, but it should be labelled as a reviewer note.
Cites SLHD as 48% from Table 3, but the results text says 58% (56/97 knee articles). A notes the Table 3 source but not this second inconsistency.

Reports isokinetic dynamometry in 73% of studies and the tldr calls it the most common test. Both come from the abstract, but the results say 44/114 (39%) and Table 3 ranks SLHD (48%) above iso-K (38%). The inconsistency is not flagged.
'Two studies addressed ankle injury' follows the abstract, but the results section says 3 studies.
Gives no benchmark values (85%/90% LSI, H:Q >70%) and does not say the suggested batteries are unvalidated.
Content is not derived from the review.

note: A catches the source's internal abstract/results discrepancies and gives benchmarks and caveats. B repeats the abstract's 73% isokinetic and 2-ankle-study figures, which conflict with the results section.
